items.quote: The world was the first figure or image of God, Man is the image of the World
items.note: Opens a chain of images: the world images God, Man images the world.

items.quote: the Zoophite or sensible hearb is the image of the Animall
items.note: The text glosses Zoophite as sensible hearb and places it in the chain below the Animall.

items.quote: the Plant is the image of the Zoophite, Mettalls are the image of the Plant, stones represent the likenesse and images of Mettalls
items.note: The chain of images runs down through Plant and Mettalls to stones.

items.quote: The great world is in every thing one with the little world, as the child with its parent
items.note: Great world and little world are said to be one in every thing; the likeness given is child and parent.

items.name: the prudent Ancients
items.quote: the prudent Ancients wilsely called Man a Microcosm or little World
items.note: The name Microcosm for Man is given as the Ancients' word.

items.quote: a Microcosm or little World, which few now a dayes understand, that the great visible World was made Man
items.note: Stated: Microcosm is glossed little World, and its sense is given as: the great visible World was made Man.

items.quote: which few now a dayes understand
items.note: The text says the sense of the name Microcosm is understood by few now; it does not say here that it is kept back.

items.quote: As the great world is bipartite, consisting of two parts, visible and invisible, so also the little world man is twofold, visible in respect of his Body, invisible in respect of his Spirit.
items.note: Man is twofold as the great world is: visible Body, invisible Spirit.

items.quote: one a syderiall Spirit from the Firmament, the other from the breath of life, which is the Intellectuall Soul inspired from God, and the mouth of the most High
items.note: Two Spirits in Man with their sources: a syderiall one from the Firmament, and one from the breath of life, here called the Intellectuall Soul.

items.quote: The first Spirit is from the Limbus or greater world; the second from the word Fiat.
items.note: The margin gives the sources differently worded: first Spirit from the Limbus or greater world, second from the word Fiat.

items.quote: Man hath three parts, a mortall Body with a Syderiall Spirit, and an immortall Soule, which is the cottage of the Image of God or of the holy Spirit in Man.
items.note: Three parts of Man are counted; the Soule is called the cottage of the Image of God or of the holy Spirit.

items.quote: Angelicall according to which he is to live, and Animall which is not to be regarded
items.note: The margin names two wisdoms in Man, Angelicall and Animall, and says which he is to live by. A one-letter gap stands earlier in this note.

items.quote: Regeneration overcometh a bad birth.
items.note: A margin sentence on Regeneration; the lines given do not explain it further.

items.quote: If a man live sensually by his own proper and proud Will according to flesh and blood onely, he is but a Brute or Beast
items.note: First of three ways of living: sensually, by which a man is a Brute or Beast.

items.name: Scripture
items.quote: (according to those Epithites in Scripture) he be a Dog, Fox, Wolfe, Sheep, Sow, or generation of Vipers
items.note: The beast names for such a man are given as Scripture's Epithites.

items.quote: of which I shall discourse more at large in my Treatise of Signatures
items.note: The author points to another writing of his own, his Treatise of Signatures, for more on this.

items.quote: and therefore shall forbear to speak more thereof at this time
items.note: The author says he holds back more on this matter here; the reason he gives is that he treats it in the other treatise.

items.quote: If he live Rationally, then he is a Man
items.note: Second way of living: Rationally, by which he is a Man.

items.quote: hath dominion over the living Creatures in his body
items.note: The one who lives Rationally is given dominion over the living Creatures in his body.

items.quote: The invisible or immortall body of Man from the breath of God is not subject to Stars or Astronomers.
items.note: The margin speaks of an invisible or immortall body from the breath of God, not subject to Stars or Astronomers.

items.quote: if he live, according to the God-like Spirit, upon the Tree of Life, observing the property of the Image of God
items.note: Third way of living: according to the God-like Spirit, upon the Tree of Life.

items.quote: if (I say) he live according to the Talent and Treasure laid up in his Earthen Vessell and committed to him
items.note: With (I say) the author restates living upon the Tree of Life in other figures: Talent, Treasure, Earthen Vessell. Interpreted (mine): the restating shows these are figures for one thing; the lines given do not say plainly what.

items.quote: then hath he dominion over the Stars and all things else
items.note: The one who lives by the God-like Spirit has dominion over the Stars and all things else.

items.quote: Man comprehends and carryeth all things about in himselfe; whereof he is made that beareth he in himselfe
items.note: Man carries in himself all things, because he bears what he is made of.

items.quote: He was made of the world, he beareth the world about in him, and is borne of the world.
items.note: Three relations of Man to the world: made of it, bearing it, borne of it.

items.quote: the first matter (which was a kind of ineffigiate confused Essence, which Phylosophers call the Chaos and Hylen, or Mother of the world)
items.note: The text says what the first matter was: a kind of ineffigiate confused Essence.

items.name: Phylosophers
items.quote: which Phylosophers call the Chaos and Hylen, or Mother of the world
items.note: The names Chaos, Hylen and Mother of the world are given as the Phylosophers' names for the first matter.

items.quote: was the seed of the great world, so the great world is the seed of Adam or Man
items.note: First matter is seed of the great world; the great world is seed of Adam or Man.

items.quote: so Man (Adam) lay hid in the world
items.note: The text says Man lay hid in the world, as the world was hid in the Waters. It is a hiding of one thing in another, not of a teaching.

items.quote: Water is the Matrix of the world, upon which the Spirit of God moved, Gen. 1.
items.note: The margin calls Water the Matrix of the world and names Gen. 1 beside it.

items.name: 2 Pet. 3.5
items.quote: The Earth plung'd or swam up out of the Water, 2 Pet. 3.5.
items.note: The margin names 2 Pet. 3.5 for the Earth coming up out of the Water, beside the passage on the world hid in the Waters.

items.quote: The first matter was made a world, and the great World was made Man.
items.note: Two makings in a row: first matter into a world, the great World into Man.

items.quote: As a Tree groweth from the seed, the seed is the beginning of the Tree, and the seed also is the end of the Tree
items.note: The likeness of Tree and seed: the seed is both beginning and end.

items.quote: for in every graine or seed of the Tree there lies hid another Tree
items.note: The text says another Tree lies hid in every seed; again a hiding of thing in thing.

items.name: Paracelsus
items.quote: the First Matter (which Paracelsus calleth the Limbus, whose Earth was the WORD of the Lord) was the seed of all things that were to be created
items.note: Limbus is given as Paracelsus' name for the First Matter, the seed of all things to be created.

items.quote: which Paracelsus calleth the Limbus
items.note: Here the Limbus is the First Matter, which this paragraph makes the seed of the great world; N101 says the Limbus or greater world, as one thing.

items.quote: so God extracted every creature out of the first matter
items.note: The margin says every creature was extracted by God out of the first matter, likened to a craftsman's shapes. A one-letter gap stands earlier in this note.

items.quote: Man was the last of all as the perfect seed, which againe is able out of himselfe to beget another Man like himself
items.note: Man is the last created and is called the perfect seed.

items.quote: And though Man be not a seed as other seed is, yet hath he power to cast seed out of himselfe
items.note: Stated: the text itself says Man is not a seed as other seed is, so seed said of Man is not meant as of other seed.

items.quote: so every one that is borne of him bears about him that which he did, viz. the whole world
items.note: Every one born of Adam bears the whole world as Adam did.

items.quote: all men are but one man, of flesh, blood, and spirit
items.note: All men are said to be one man.

items.quote: that Earth or field which hath all seeds in it self
items.note: The margin calls Man the Earth or field that has all seeds in itself. A one-letter gap stands just before these words.

items.quote: As the Son is not lesser then his Father, so Man is not lesser then the World.
items.note: The margin says Man is not lesser than the World.

items.quote: Therefore the knowledge of Man is to be taken from both Lights, as the Son cannot be known from himselfe alone but from his Father.
items.note: Knowledge of Man is to be taken from both Lights. The lines given do not name the two here; MICRO.21 names the Light of Nature.

items.quote: Man hath two Fathers, an Eternall whose Image he beareth, and a Mortall one, which is the whole world with all the creatures
items.note: Two Fathers of Man: an Eternall one, and a Mortall one which is the whole world.

items.quote: that Limus Terrae, that slime of the earth, or hidden Secret thing
items.note: Limus Terrae is glossed slime of the earth and is set equal, by that is, to the mortal Father, the whole world with all the creatures.

items.quote: or hidden Secret thing
items.note: The text calls the Limus Terrae a hidden Secret thing.

items.quote: the most precious Esse or Being of all creatures, which all Phylosophers, Physitians Astronomers, and Divines are to consider and diligently inquire into
items.note: The same thing is called the most precious Esse or Being of all creatures, and four kinds of men are told to inquire into it.

items.quote: None can know the image unlesse he first know him whose image he is.
items.note: The margin gives a rule of knowing: the image is known only through him whose image it is.

items.name: Hermes
items.quote: Hermes calleth Man an earthly God.
items.note: The margin gives earthly God as Hermes' name for Man.

items.name: Gen. 2.7
items.note: The margin names Gen. 2.7 beside the passage on the Limus Terrae, the slime of the earth.

items.quote: there is no member or part that doth not answer to some Element, some Planet, some Intelligence or other
items.note: Every member or part of Man answers to some Element, Planet or Intelligence.

items.quote: to some measure and number in the Archetype or first pattern
items.note: Archetype is glossed first pattern.

items.quote: Man hath a visible body from the Elements as a fit garment and sutable cottage for the Soul
items.note: The visible body is from the Elements and is garment and cottage for the Soul.

items.quote: Aetheriall and Astrall Body or chariot and vehicle of the Soule, wherein the Intellectuall Soul and earthy Body like two Extreams are knit, glued and confederate together
items.note: The invisible body from the Heaven or Firmament is called chariot and vehicle of the Soule, and joins Soul and earthy Body as two Extreams.

items.quote: in this third mean which partaketh of the other two they are coupled and united into one intire man
items.note: The astral body is a third mean partaking of the other two.

items.quote: The perfection and dignity of Man.
items.what: The perfection and dignity of Man
items.note: A margin heading set beside the passage on the invisible body.

items.quote: Thus God and Man cannot be united but by a Mean, even our Saviour who partaketh of two Natures, the Caelestiall and Terrestriall, the Divine & Humane.
items.note: The margin sets a likeness beside the Medium of soul and body: God and Man united by a Mean, our Saviour of two Natures.

items.name: Paracelsus
items.quote: is infused by God into the Elementary body through the Astra's as a Medium
items.note: The margin gives as Paracelsus' saying that the soul is infused into the Elementary body through the Astra's as a Medium. Two one-letter gaps stand just before these words.

items.quote: Through this Medium, this middle Aetheriall little body
items.note: Medium is here the middle Aetheriall little body.

items.quote: by the command of God, who is the Centre of the great world, and by the imploying of his Intelligences or Spirits to that end
items.note: God is called the Centre of the great world; the soul's descent is by his command and by his Intelligences or Spirits.

items.quote: is first poured and descendeth into the middle poynt of the Heart, which is the Centre of the little world
items.note: The Intellectuall Soule first descends into the Heart, called the Centre of the little world.

items.quote: by which heat it joyneth to the Spirit begotten from the heart, by the spirit it drencheth it selfe into the blood, by the blood it cleaveth to all the members
items.note: The steps by which the soul reaches the members: vehicle to naturall heat, heat to Spirit, spirit to blood, blood to members.

items.quote: it holds and keeps the same course with that of the Firmament, whose operations it draweth to it selfe by a peculiar magnetick vertue, just as the visible body doth the efficacy of the Elements
items.note: The Aethereall body follows the course of the Firmament and draws its operations by a magnetick vertue.

items.quote: and so remaineth one (thing) with the visible and invisible world
items.note: The Aethereall body remains one with the visible and invisible world; the word thing stands in brackets in the text.

items.name: John 10.30
items.quote: John 10.30.
items.note: The margin names John 10.30 where the text says one with the world as the Son with his Father.

items.quote: The whole Firmament is in us with the Planets and Stars
items.note: The whole Firmament with Planets and Stars is said to be in us.

items.quote: so doth the Stars with all their properties pierce into Man, so that of the syderiall spirit of the Firmament we may learn all Naturall things.
items.note: The Stars pierce into Man; from the syderiall spirit all Naturall things may be learned.

items.quote: The MIND.
items.note: A margin heading set at the end of MICRO.18, before the paragraph on the Intellectuall and immortal Soul.

items.quote: or Spirit by the inbreathing of God, created (with the four foresaid inhabitants of the Elements, which the bruit beasts have not) after the Image of God and the Divine Triunity
items.note: The Intellectuall Soul or Spirit is by God's inbreathing, created after the Image of God and the Divine Triunity.

items.quote: the four foresaid inhabitants of the Elements
items.note: The word foresaid points back to an earlier place in this writing; the lines given do not include it.

items.name: Zach. 12.1; Gen. 2.7; Es. 42.5; Wisd. 2.23
items.note: The margin names four places of Scripture beside the Intellectuall and immortal Soul.

items.quote: that so in all things he might be one with his Heavenly Father, who is in us by his Spirit
items.note: The end named for this creation: that Man be one with his Heavenly Father, who is in us by his Spirit.

items.quote: from which we learn sacred Divinity and all heavenly and earthly secrets without errour
items.note: The text speaks of heavenly and earthly secrets and says they are learned from the Spirit of the Father in us.

items.name: 1 John 2.27; Chap. 4.14; Acts 17.28
items.quote: 1 John 2.27. Chap. 4.14. Acts 17.28.
items.note: The margin names these places beside the sentence that ends: in him we are, and live, and are moved.

items.quote: As God is One in Essence, Trine (or Three) in persons, so Man is One in Person, Trine (or Three) in distinct Essence
items.note: God and Man are set in mirrored order: one Essence and three persons; one Person and three Essences.

items.quote: composed Triune, of a Terrene Body, an Aethereall Spirit of the Heavens, and a living vivifying Soule which God breathed into him, and is the house of God
items.note: Stated: what Triune means of Man: Terrene Body, Aethereall Spirit, and Soule, which is the house of God.

items.name: the holy Scripture
items.quote: This the holy Scripture witnesseth
items.note: The threefold make of Man is said to be witnessed by the holy Scripture.

items.quote: Unitrine or Triune, One in Three, or Three in One
items.note: Unitrine or Triune is glossed One in Three, or Three in One.

items.name: all that truly professed Phylosophy from the Light of Nature
items.quote: As also the unanimous consent of all that truly professed Phylosophy from the Light of Nature.
items.note: A second witness is named beside Scripture: those who professed Phylosophy from the Light of Nature.

items.name: Luke 1.47; 1 Thes. 5.23; Gen. 2.7
items.note: The margin names the places of Scripture meant by the witness.

items.name: Rhunrad
items.quote: of Rhunrad worthy of perpetuall memory
items.note: The margin sends the reader to a writing of Rhunrad; its title has a one-letter gap in the text given.

items.name: Paul
items.quote: Paul the greatest Phylosopher and Divine shewes three parts of Man, Spirit, Soule and Body.
items.note: The three parts are given as Paul's, in the order Spirit, Soule and Body.

items.quote: There are two Souls or two Spirits in Man, Mortall from the first matter which is the life of the body, and Immortall from God.
items.note: The margin says two Souls or two Spirits, the mortal one from the first matter; MICRO.14 gives the first as from the Firmament and N101 as from the Limbus or greater world.

items.quote: The Spirit is the Life of the Soule, the Spirit and Soule are the life of the body. John 14.
items.note: An order of life among the three: Spirit to Soule, both to body; John 14 is named beside it.

items.name: any that deny these three parts
items.quote: If happily there should be any that deny these three parts
items.note: The author names possible deniers of the three parts and answers them with what they must still acknowledge.

items.quote: Man was created è Limo Terrae, out of the clay or dust of the Earth, by the word FIAT
items.note: Here the Limus Terrae is glossed the clay or dust of the Earth; MICRO.17 glosses it slime of the earth.

items.quote: an eternall Spirit or breath of life from the mouth of God, which is that Linum Caelorum, or slime of the Heavens from the Lord
items.note: The eternal Spirit or breath of life is named Linum Caelorum, glossed slime of the Heavens.

items.quote: The Limus Terrae, or dust of the Earth, is two-fold, visible and invisible
items.note: The Limus Terrae is said to be two-fold.

items.quote: He hath his Body or cottage from the Earth and Water; but the life that dwells therein is from the Aire and Firmament of Fire
items.note: The four are divided: Body from Earth and Water, life from Aire and Firmament of Fire.

items.quote: which life is the Syderiall Spirit, and is properly the Man, not flesh and blood
items.note: Stated: the Syderiall Spirit is the life dwelling in the body, and is properly the Man.

items.quote: As the Syderiall Spirit is the life of the Body, so the Spirit of the Lord is the life of the Intellectuall Soule.
items.note: A proportion: Syderiall Spirit to Body as Spirit of the Lord to Intellectuall Soule.

items.quote: as the Sydereall Spirit dwells in the Body and works therein day and night, for this invisible is himselfe the Firmament
items.note: The Sydereall Spirit works in the Body day and night and is itself called the Firmament.

items.quote: so the Spirit of the Lord, the WORD of God, the eternall man dwells in the Soule: the house is the habitation of the Soule, the Soule is the habitation and cottage of God
items.note: Spirit of the Lord, WORD of God and eternall man are named together as dwelling in the Soule; a ladder of dwellings follows.

items.quote: God created Man to be his Tabernacle as well in this as in the world to come.
items.note: The margin says Man was created to be God's Tabernacle in this world and the next.

items.quote: the most compleat figure of the world, and expresse image of God, in whom he rested from creating
items.note: Man is the most complete figure of the world and express image of God, in whom God rested.

items.quote: when (I say) he was on the sixt day made up of all things, the last of the Creatures, and image not onely of the eternall God, but also of the great world
items.note: Man was made on the sixt day, of all things, last, and as image both of God and of the great world.

items.quote: it followeth that there are three worlds or Heavens in Man, and that he is born about of three Worlds, or rather is all the world, and a most sure and undoubted Pattern of the whole Universe.
items.note: The conclusion drawn: three worlds or Heavens in Man; he is all the world and Pattern of the Universe.

items.name: Manilus
items.quote: Exemplumque Dei quisque est in imagine parvâ, Manilus.
items.note: A Latin line is given under the name Manilus beside the conclusion; the note does not English it.

items.quote: That which is Naturated savoureth of the Nature of that which did Naturate it.
items.note: A margin rule: the thing Naturated tastes of what Naturated it.

items.quote: God dwelleth in the Soul as in the Heaven of Man.
items.note: The margin calls the Soul the Heaven of Man, where God dwells.

items.name: some
items.quote: And therefore some have called him the Fourth World, in whom are found all those things that are in the other three
items.note: The name Fourth World for Man is given as what some have called him.

items.quote: for which cause also he may be called by the name of every Creature
items.note: Because all is found in him, Man may bear the name of every Creature; MICRO.15 names beasts he is known by.

items.quote: for what else is the Spirit of Man which God breathed into him but God himselfe dwelling in us?
items.note: The Spirit or Mind of Man is said to be God himself dwelling in us.

items.quote: The invisible Body or true Internall Man consisting of Reason and an Astrall Spirit, agreeth with the Angells, and is their fellow
items.note: Stated: the invisible Body or true Internall Man consists of Reason and an Astrall Spirit, and is fellow of the Angells.

items.quote: And if he be a true Magician, he is not inferiour to the Angells in all Magicall operation, and is Lord and Possessor of all things.
items.note: On a condition, being a true Magician, Man equals the Angells in Magicall operation. The lines given do not say what a true Magician is.

items.quote: His mortall Phisicall Body he hath from the frame of the world and all things created therein, for all Externall things are nothing else but the Body of Man.
items.note: The mortal body is from the frame of the world; all Externall things are called the Body of Man.

items.quote: of the Archetype or God-like world in God, of the Intellible or Angellicall, of the sensible Elementall or corporall world
items.note: The three worlds Man partakes of are named one by one.

items.quote: hath a symbolicall operation and conversation with them all
items.note: Man's operation and conversation with the three worlds is called symbolicall; the lines given do not explain the word.

items.quote: So that he partaketh of a threefold world
items.note: Here the worlds are counted three; the numbered heads that follow at once run from 1 to 5, with Firmament and Stars, Elements, and Elemented things as separate heads.

items.quote: 1. He communicateth with God in his Soule or Mind, because by the breath of life he was made after his image
items.note: First of five numbered heads (1 to 5, MICRO.25 to MICRO.29), each naming something Man shares in.

items.quote: the Intellectuall Soul is a certaine particle of the Divine Soule
items.note: Stated: the Intellectuall Soul is a particle of the Divine Soule.

items.quote: in which very Soule God hath sowen certaine seeds and resemblances of his Mind in us, much like to that of an Eccho which sends back its voyce from the resemblance of the aire
items.note: God has sown seeds and resemblances of his Mind in the Soule; the likeness given is an Eccho.

items.quote: The mind raised up into the most High God and united with him converseth with God, and doth the same works
items.note: The mind raised and united with God converses with him and does the same works.

items.quote: neither is there any thing in God which very thing is not represented in Man
items.note: Every thing in God is said to be represented in Man.

items.quote: Stern-man of the Soul or Rationall Spirit, & like the eternall God concludeth all Beings, Times and Places
items.note: The margin says what the Mind is: driver or Stern-man of the Soul or Rationall Spirit. A gap of foreign script follows the word Mind, and a one-letter gap stands before these words.

items.quote: He hath a semblance with the Angells in respect of the invisible Body and Rationall Soul
items.note: Second head: likeness with the Angells by the invisible Body and Rationall Soul; the sentence adds that he has the same wisdome they have.

items.quote: he is Gabalis socius Angelorum, a curdled companion of the Angells, or one mixed with in fellowship
items.note: A Latin name for Man is given and Englished two ways: a curdled companion of the Angells, or one mixed with in fellowship.

items.quote: He participateth with the Firmament and Stars of whom he received that Astrall body or Syderiall Spirit, which is the true Astrall Man
items.note: Third head: Astrall body and Syderiall Spirit are named as one, received from Firmament and Stars, and called the true Astrall Man.

items.quote: for flesh and blood is not the Man, but the Spirit contained in them
items.note: The Man is the Spirit contained in flesh and blood, not flesh and blood; MICRO.23 says the same.

items.quote: which Astrall Spirit is the subject of humane Reason that containeth the sences and wisdome in it
items.note: Stated: the Astrall Spirit is the subject of humane Reason and holds the sences and wisdome.

items.quote: and is made (Animall) a living creature with the body
items.note: The word Animall stands in brackets beside its Englishing, a living creature: the text marks the sense in which the word is used.

items.quote: This Spirit and the Astra's are but one thing in Man, but the body is the subject of this Spirit
items.note: The Astrall Spirit and the Astra's are one thing in Man; the body is its subject.

items.quote: and so the Astra's rule man in the Spirit, and the Spirit of a man ruleth the Body in flesh and blood
items.note: An order of rule: Astra's over the Spirit, Spirit over the Body. MICRO.16 gives dominion over the Stars to the one who lives by the God-like Spirit.

items.quote: This Spirit is mortall; onely the Intellectuall Soule which God breathed into man is immortall.
items.note: The Astrall Spirit is mortal; only the Intellectuall Soule is immortal.

items.quote: This Spirit is mortall
items.note: Here the Astrall body or Syderiall Spirit, from Firmament and Stars, is mortal, and MICRO.17 calls the body from the Firmament invisible; N103 speaks of the invisible or immortall body of Man from the breath of God.

items.quote: He partaketh of the Elements, for from these he had his mortall Physicall Earthy body
items.note: Fourth head: the mortal body is from the Elements.

items.name: Paracelsus
items.quote: the world, which is the Parant of Man according to Paracelsus
items.note: That the world is the Parant of Man is given as according to Paracelsus.

items.quote: the four Elementary Spirits of the four inhabitants of the world, as also the fift kind of Flages of a thousand sorts incorporated into the Soule of the Microcosm
items.note: Five kinds of Spirits are counted: four Elementary Spirits and a fifth kind, Flages. The lines given do not say what Flages are.

items.quote: the Imagination also of these five Spirits in the Elements must be in the Microcosm Man
items.note: The Imagination of the five Spirits must be in Man.

items.quote: the use of Mans Reason according to the will and command of God, is as a Chaine were with those five Spirits are knit and bound together that they may acquiesce with his Imagination
items.note: Reason used by God's will is likened to a Chaine binding the five Spirits so that they agree with Man's Imagination.

items.quote: He partaketh of all Elemented Animalls, Vegetables and Mineralls; for he hath in him the Nature and properties of all these.
items.note: Fifth head: Man has the nature and properties of Animalls, Vegetables and Mineralls.

items.quote: All things were made of nothing and Man was made of all those things.
items.note: The margin: all things from nothing, Man from all things.

items.quote: All things were made of nothing
items.note: This note says all things were made of nothing; MICRO.17 makes the First Matter the seed of all things to be created, and N105 says God extracted every creature out of the first matter.

items.quote: The great world was the matrix of Adam, thus the whole frame of the world is the mother of all things that are brought forth.
items.note: The great world is the matrix of Adam; N104 calls Water the Matrix of the world.

items.quote: Man therefore who was the last is the most excellent and noble of all Creatures, because he hath the parts of the whole world
items.note: The conclusion of the five heads: Man, the last, is the most excellent creature because he has the parts of the whole world.

items.quote: nor is there any thing in the great world which may not really be found in man
items.note: Every thing of the great world is said to be really found in man; the weight lies on the word really.

items.quote: The Son is like the father in all things, the father being known the Son is known also.
items.note: The rule of Son and father is repeated: knowing the father gives knowledge of the Son.

items.quote: Man the greatest miracle of Nature & most admirable Extract & kernell of the four Elements
items.note: Man is called Extract and kernell of the four Elements.

items.quote: is truly every Creature, for he is all the world
items.note: Man is truly every Creature, being all the world.

items.quote: he alone hath this honor to have semblance with all things, and operation with all, and conuersation with all
items.note: Man alone has likeness, operation and conversation with all things.

items.quote: Yea he riseth to such perfection that he is made the Son of God, transformed into the same image which is God and made one with him
items.note: The highest step named: Man made the Son of God, transformed into the image which is God, one with him.

items.quote: which is not granted either to Angells, or the world, or any other Creature, but to Man only that he should become the Son of God, and be united to God
items.note: This union is granted to Man only, not to Angells, the world or any other Creature.

items.name: John 17.11, 12.22, 23
items.note: The margin names places in John beside Man made one with God.
